page: Amazon Web Services i7i.48xlarge is a storage-optimized bare-metal-equivalent instance running on the AWS Nitro System. It is powered by 5th Generation Intel Xeon 8559C processors delivering 96 physical cores and 192 dedicated vCPUs at a base clock speed of 3.2 GHz. The x86_64 platform features 320 MB of shared L3 cache and supports Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) along with AVX-512 vector instruction sets. Memory is provisioned with 1,536 GB of DDR5 operating at 6 GHz, achieving a balanced 8 GB per vCPU allocation.

Storage and throughput subsystems are designed for high-volume disk-intensive workloads. The instance bundles 45,000 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, paired with 100 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. In synthetic and platform benchmarks, the server ranks in the top tier for multi-core compute, delivering 169,956.68 on stress-ng and 131,162.12 on PassMark CPU tests. The memory architecture produces 569.6 GB/sec in uncached read bandwidth and 238.51 GB/sec in write bandwidth.

Benchmark results for application workloads confirm top-tier performance for I/O and data processing, logging 205.98 million operations per second on Redis SET tasks, 35,982.5 on PassMark database tests, and 210.03 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. On single-core CPU metrics, performance sits within standard enterprise percentiles. CPU-driven inference tests via AMX demonstrate top-tier prompt processing and text generation speeds for medium and large language model architectures without dedicated GPU accelerators.

Amazon Web Services i7i.48xlarge delivers high resource density by packing 45 TB of direct-attached NVMe storage, massive DDR5 memory, and 192 vCPUs onto a single system image. It is suited for large distributed databases, high-throughput in-memory stores, big data analytics engines, data warehousing, and I/O-heavy ETL pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services i7i.48xlarge is a storage-optimized instance built on the Nitro System, featuring 96 physical cores and 192 vCPUs from Intel Xeon 8559C processors running at 3.2 GHz. The system provides 1,536 GB of high-frequency DDR5 memory, a baseline network bandwidth of 100 Gbps, and 45,000 GB of attached local NVMe SSD storage. Benchmark evaluations show top-tier multi-core compute capability, high uncached memory bandwidth exceeding 569 GB/sec, and high throughput on database operations, including over 205 million Redis SET operations per second. While single-thread performance is balanced in the median range, hardware acceleration flags such as AMX and AVX-512 facilitate efficient vector computing and CPU-based machine learning inference. The instance represents an integrated solution for I/O-intensive database engines, distributed caching systems, large-scale search clusters, and heavy ETL data warehousing workloads.
